messages:
ashok: noticing sustained egress congestion in eu-west when H200 pods hit ~2k concurrent streams — packet drops and tail latency rising.
infra-bot: [alert] network-egress-high eu-west — 10.3 Gbps avg, 0.18% packet drop over 10m window.
maria: is traffic mostly prod or evals?
ashok: ~70% non-prod evals + a handful of heavy customer canaries from churned load tests.
devon: can we gate evals? earlier we had a windowed-run flag for bulk evals.
maria: yes, but canaries are tricky. suggest: slice traffic by priority and route low-priority to cheaper/less-peak hardware (L40S) or H100.
lee: also seeing memory oversubscription on some H200 instances when we switch to int8 kernels for the new model. that increases retransmits.
sre-oncall: short-term mitigations: 1) apply per-VPC egress QoS, 2) throttle batch_size from 128->64 for H200 serving, 3) rate-limit canary jobs.
ashok: agree. do we have routing rules we can update quickly? want soft-fallback: prefer H200, if egress > 8Gbps or latency > 120ms fallback to H100/L40S.
maria: we can implement in routing policy. example pseudo-config:
```
route_policy:
  priority: [prod, canary, eval]
  prefer: H200
  fallback:
    - condition: egress>8Gbps or tail_latency>120ms
      to: [H100, L40S]
    - condition: region==eu-west and maintenance==true
      to: [H100, us-east]
```
procurement: FYI: H200 lead time is still ~10-12 weeks for committed reservations; H100 similar, L40S inventory is available in 2-3 weeks for immediate purchase.
devon: cost reminder: per-hour raw costs: H200 >> H100 > L40S, but L40S higher token-per-second latency increases per-token cost. need throughput projections to quantify.
lee: we should run a quick projection: if we offload 25% of non-prod to L40S, what happens to overall egress and token cost? anyone have the last 7d distribution?
ashok: attaching quick numbers: last_7d_total_tokens=1.8B, non-prod=520M, avg_tps_nonprod=220, peak_egress=11Gbps.
maria: propose experiment: 48h slice — route 30% eval to L40S, 20% to H100, monitor tail latency, throughput, and egress. if egress drops below 8Gbps keep; else revert.
sre-oncall: I'll add a retention SLA for metrics and set alert if token cost delta > +12% or user-facing latency > +10%.
procurement: If experiment shows sustained demand, we should lock a small H200 buffer (4-8 units) to cover peak windows — can convert later. estimate capex impact in next cycle.
devon: also consider KV cache placement — copying large caches to H100 nodes could reduce egress if we colocate evals.
lee: good point. and check kernel selection flags — maybe fallback to non-int8 kernels on H200 during congestion to reduce memory pressure at slight perf hit.
ashok: action items:
- sre-oncall: apply QoS + set alerts (ETA 1h)
- maria + devon: schedule 48h slice experiment (start in 2h)
- lee: validate kernel/memory settings and provide safe fallback (ETA EOD)
- procurement: prepare 4-unit H200 buffer quote and ETA (tomorrow)
infra-bot: maintenance scheduled in eu-west tomorrow 02:00-04:00 UTC. will increase risk window.
maria: thanks — will circle back with experiment config and a rollforward/rollback plan.
devon: adding me and ashok to runbook updates.
ashok: thanks everyone. we'll re-evaluate after the slice run. :thumbsup:
